Introduction

Artificial intelligence (AI; more precisely, [machine learning, {particularly (deep learning, [notably neural networks, {including transformer-based systems}])}]) has transformed research across computer science and related disciplines. Recent advances have improved the performance of systems that perceive language, images, and structured data, while also raising important questions about reliability, alignment, and evaluation.

This paper examines the methodological and conceptual foundations of modern AI research. It reviews representative approaches, identifies open challenges, and proposes a framework for assessing progress in a way that is both technically rigorous and broadly applicable. The central aim is to clarify how current systems can be understood, compared, and responsibly developed.
